svg.text: Direction B, "festival smithy": the same stations, chunkier and brighter
Same scale, layout and kept parts as Direction A (1 stud = 28 px). Thicker posts and trim, rounded corners, toy-like outlines, red lacquer and gold, teal tiles, lanterns and blossom.

g.text: stand 2
Ore shrine
red-and-white rope, gold tray, big
sparkly ore, chunky lever with a gold ball
Forge
arched glowing mouth, gold lintel, teal
chimney cap, round lantern, pebble plinth
Anvil
rounded block, barrel base with gold
hoops; face still matte and dark
Hilt Bench
gold-framed board of bright grips and
tsuba, round lamp, red-edged tatami
Sword holders
red-lacquer pedestals with gold caps,
blossom tree by the shop front
5.2-stud player

svg.text: Street view (same building as Direction A)

g.text: 刀鍛冶
• Posts and trim 20–30% thicker, corners rounded,
dark outlines (in Studio: darker edge parts).
• Warm orange cedar instead of near-black timber;
cream plaster; teal tiles with gold ridge ends.
• Red lacquer and gold on holders, lintels, sign.
• A lantern on every post, red noren, blossom tree,
flower pots, moss along the ground.
• Brighter sky and greener hills.
• Layout, sizes, every scripted part, the forging camera.
• The anvil face stays matte and dark, so the blade
still pops. B is busier around it than A.
B is more eye-catching and closer to Create Pottery!.
A matches the Japanese Village concept art and keeps
the background calmer behind the blade.
